transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’m useless now and just letting everyone down since my fall. Ever since my knee procedure, I haven't been able to do any of my usual activities or volunteering, and I just feel like I'm dead weight to everyone who was counting on me.

Since your knee procedure, have you been feeling down or unable to enjoy things most of the day nearly every day, even when you’re not thinking about your limitations? About how long has that been going on?

Yes, I've been feeling completely down and just can't find joy in anything anymore—even my hiking, gardening, and workshops just leave me feeling blank and indifferent. This has been going on steadily for about a month now, starting a couple of weeks after my knee procedure when I realized I wasn't bouncing back.

When there are moments you’re not focused on your knee recovery or the changes since surgery, does the sadness still stay with you most of the day? Or does it mainly flare up when you think about those stressors?

It's pretty constant, honestly. It feels like a persistent cloud hanging over me all day, even when I'm not actively thinking about my knee or the surgery. It doesn't just flare up; that heavy feeling is just always there in the background.
Over this past month, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? If so, which of these have been happening?

Yes, I've been dealing with all of those; I lie awake worrying only to wake up exhausted at 4 a.m., and I have to force myself to eat even a piece of toast. My body feels so heavy that simple chores feel like climbing a mountain, and my mind is so foggy that even deciding what to wear is overwhelming. I've also had quiet thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning, though I haven't made any plans to do anything.

How much have these symptoms affected your day-to-day functioning—for example, are you still able to manage basic self-care, household tasks, and appointments, or are you struggling to keep up with those too?

It has completely disrupted my daily life; I've gone from running community workshops to canceling almost everything. Even basic chores like tidying the kitchen or taking a shower feel like climbing a mountain because of how exhausted I am. I've even started avoiding my friends' calls because managing any of it just feels completely overwhelming.
